title: Constellation Strategy Unveil — All Hands
summary: Leadership unveiled the 'Constellation' multi-product strategy focused on embedding-first features, regional private deployments, and reliability margins for Q1. Key priorities: shipping embedding-first SDKs, expanding Redwood Dedicated capacity in EMEA, strengthening SOC/ISO posture for Private customers, and three operational 'bets' to reduce per-token costs. Cross-functional asks were made to Product, Infra, and Sales. Q&A surfaced concerns about hiring runway, rollout timeline, and benchmarking plans.
next_steps: Maya to share Constellation one-pager and OKR mapping (by 2026-11-27)
Product to publish embedding SDK roadmap and alpha sign-up form (by 2026-12-03)
Infra to circulate Dedicated capacity runbook for EMEA launch (by 2026-12-10)
Security to post SOC2/ISO gap summary and customer-facing FAQ (by 2026-12-01)
action_items: Lina - Draft embedding SDK alpha signup and starter guide - due 2026-12-03
Samir - EMEA Dedicated capacity estimate + cost model - due 2026-12-10
Ethan - Run early QPS benchmark against quantized variants and share results - due 2026-12-08
Grace - Update hiring cadence and redisplay candidacy plan by org - due 2026-11-30
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-24 18:30 UTC
Duration: ~74 minutes
Attendees: leadership team + company wide (rumored ~210)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. This one is a bit of a long one, we want to lay out a multi-quarter plan we're calling 'Constellation'. Um, quick energy check — hope you had coffee.
[00:30] Audience: claps, occasional hi's
[01:05] Maya: Quick headline version: three product vectors — embedding-first (APIs and SDKs), Dedicated capacity expansion for EMEA, and Private / compliance hardening. These are the bets to get us to steady unit economics and enterprise traction.
[02:12] Ethan: I'll start with some numbers, sorry if I stutter — we ran a set of internal benchmarks in October, trying to get consistent p99 tail behavior across 2k token contexts. We saw consistent latency improvements with our new batching heuristics but cost per token is still the lever we need to pull.
[03:05] Speaker 1: (inaudible) did you say 2K or 20K?
[03:08] Ethan: 2K, yeah, 2K typical. Some of the tail runs used extended contexts, but our focus is the typical 2K window for product first.
[04:00] Lina: On product side, embedding-first means we will ship SDKs that treat embeddings as first-class, low-latency operations — client-side batching, streaming similarity scores, and a small on-disk cache. We're providing opinionated defaults for tooling so customers don't hand-roll naive loops.
[04:45] Lina: There's also a partner program, starting with two vector db partners, so we can provide end-to-end examples. Docs will be out in early December.
[05:30] Audience: um, claps
[06:10] Maya: We talked about Dedicated capacity in Q3; now we accelerate EMEA launch to early Q1. Reason: customer demand from gaming and fintech segments, and regulatory residency asks. Samir will talk about infra work.
[07:00] Samir: EMEA expansion is two parts: capacity (GPU pools) and deployment automation for private control planes. We're leaning into reserved pools so latency is predictable. Note — this will require careful cost modeling; we plan to present a commit vs. spot blended model.
[08:05] Audience/Crosstalk: questions about pricing buckets and burst logic
[09:00] Ethan: On the runtime side, the 'graceful degradation' story has to be tighter. We're building fallbacks — quantized variants, cross-region routing, and smaller model tiers. Some transcription notes: k-vcache sometimes comes out as kayvee cache in logs, so docs will need a pass.
[10:04] Speaker 2: is there a plan for on-prem?
[10:10] Maya: Yes — Private remains a key enterprise motion. We plan a 'Private Ready' checklist: KMS/HSM integration, audit log exports, and hardened install images for air-gapped installs. Security will publish the checklist.
[11:00] Grace: Hiring is a big ask — we need infra SREs, a couple of senior infra engineers for kernels and quantization, and more product managers for embedding use-cases. We'll be moving some role prioritization into the org board this week.
[12:00] Audience: murmurs, a question about runway and spend
[12:20] Maya: Short answer — we have runway but we are disciplined on spend. The Constellation plan is designed to increase committed revenue streams (Dedicated/Private) and improve unit economics to give us room on hiring.
[13:45] Q&A Segment — mixed attendees, some voicemails:
[14:00] Speaker 3: How soon for alpha SDK?
[14:05] Lina: Alpha signups open by Dec 3, internal demo Dec 15.
[15:30] Speaker 4: Will the embedding SDK require changes to model catalog?
[15:33] Lina: Minimal — we'll surface embedding-optimized weights and a set of prepackaged transformations. Some models will get quantization profiles.
[16:40] Speaker 5: Security question — SOC2 status?
[16:45] Maya: We finished the remediation plan; auditing timeline is Q1 finish. We'll publish a public FAQ and an interim attestation for customers.
[18:00] Ethan: Operational bets to reduce per-token cost — three parallel experiments: smarter prefix caching, adaptive batching based on observed seq-length distribution, and tighter kernel selection heuristics. We expect a 10-20% cost reduction if all hit.
[19:20] Speaker 6: Quick clarification — is prefix caching going to affect latency?
[19:25] Ethan: It should help latency tail for repeated prompts; but worst case for cold starts we need better caching priming. There's a tradeoff.
[21:00] Audience: some cross talk and a question about benchmarks
[21:12] Ethan: We'll publish a benchmark harness and we welcome external reproducible runs. We'll also set guardrails — don't benchmark with dynamic caching turned on unless you mark it.
[22:30] Samir: On Dedicated we need to define SLA tiers. Today we have default, but enterprise needs 99.95 and a fallback policy. We'll add a canary deployment plan and canary rollback automation.
[24:00] Lina: For product teams, we will offer an 'embedding starter kit' with examples for search, recommender, and reranking.
[25:20] Audience: question about partner vector DB support (which ones?)
[25:25] Lina: initial partners are VectorStoreX and HarborDB — partnerships are contingent until legal clears them.
[26:30] Maya: Ok, shifting to organizational changes. We will create a small Constellation program team — Lina will lead the cross-functional program with a PM, an infra lead, and a GTM lead from sales. The program will run as a 3-month sprint for initial milestones.
[28:00] Grace: People ops — we will update leveling and provide transparency on role prioritization. There will be an AMA next week for hiring Qs.
[29:10] Audience: question about townhall cadence
[29:15] Maya: We'll keep monthly leadership updates and a larger quarterly townhall. This one is the 'unveil' and Q1 will be focused on execution.
[30:00] Open mic — selected questions:
[30:10] Speaker 7: Can you share the expected metrics for success?
[30:15] Maya: Yes — three KPIs: 1) committed revenue from Dedicated/Private, 2) per-token cost delta (target -15% by end of Q1), 3) embedding adoption (X internal integrations and Y external signups).
[33:05] Speaker 8: Will this change roadmap priorities?
[33:10] Lina: Some reprioritization — a few backlog items will be delayed. We'll publish a mapping doc.
[35:00] Ethan: Tech deep-dive offers — we'll host a 90-min follow-up for infra and runtime teams next Thursday. Sign-up sheet in Loom or internal calendar.
[36:20] Speaker 9: there was a note about benchmarking — will the results be public?
[36:25] Ethan: High level yes, raw harness available to partners under NDAs where required.
[37:50] Audience: applause
[38:30] Closing remarks: Maya thanks everyone and reiterates the three bets and the ask for focus.
[39:10] Maya: Please read the Constellation one-pager when I send it, add comments inline. We'll need program volunteers for alpha partners.
[40:00] Lina: Quick ask — product folks please file PRDs using the Constellation template.
[40:30] Samir: Infra will share a deployment runbook and a cost model spreadsheet.
[41:05] Q&A continues — misc clarifications, some long-winded comments cut by moderator.
[48:00] Speaker 10: Will we change pricing publicly?
[48:05] Maya: No immediate public pricing changes; we'll test pricing for Dedicated and Private with a small set of customers.
[50:00] Audience: final questions and thanks
[51:10] Maya: Recap next steps and action items, thanks all.
[51:40] Meeting ends around 18:59 UTC.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had typical errors (product names like 'KV cache' sometimes 'kay vee cache', 'Dedicated' sometimes 'dedicateded'), overlapping talk partially misattributed. Where inaudible, marked (inaudible).
